subject.title: [Bug]: codex turn watchdogs have inconsistent defer guards and no wall-clock ceiling; attempt-idle aborts long quiet native tool calls

question: Should the Codex watchdog wall-clock ceiling be derived from the effective run or terminal timeout, fixed at a new hard cap, or split out from the blocker-fix work?
rationale: Current main already preserves explicit long-run budgets, while the requested wall-clock ceiling changes runtime liveness policy and the issue has a protected maintainer label.

options.title: Derive From Effective Budget
options.body: Keep the wall-clock safety fuse, but compute it from the effective run or terminal timeout so configured long Codex runs are not cut short.

options.title: Accept A Fixed Cap
options.body: Make a fixed absolute cap the product contract and document the upgrade behavior for users with longer configured runs.

options.title: Split The Fix
options.body: Land the blocker/order/progress repairs first and keep the wall-clock ceiling as a separate maintainer-owned policy follow-up.

recommendation.title: Derive From Effective Budget
recommendation.body: Keep the wall-clock safety fuse, but compute it from the effective run or terminal timeout so configured long Codex runs are not cut short.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent app-server seam work and recurring Codex harness review history make this the best available routing candidate for the timeout-policy choice.
